196947:
Testimony of Anya Trundy, Deputy Commissioner Department of Administrative and Financial Sen/ices
Testifying in Favor
LD 2093, An Act to Codify and Update a Provision of Private and Special Law
Governing Temporary Disability for State Employees
Presented by Rep. Suzanne Salisbury
To the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government
Senator Baldacci and members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local
Government, I am Anya Trundy, Deputy Commissioner for the Department of Administrative and Financial Sen/ices. I am providing testimony in support of LD 2093.
This bill is extremely straightforward. So I'll keep it brief: LD 2093 repeals a provision of the Private and Special Laws from 1989 which governs temporaiy disability benefits for confidential state employees and enacts that provision in the Maine Revised Statutes.
This bill contains no substantive changes to the affected (or rather, unaffected) provisions;
it is simply moving them from one place to another. As a note, temporary disability benefits for classified employee are provided through Unions' income protection programs.
The reason for this minor change is simply a matter of accessibility for those confidential
employees who may have cause to reference this law. By moving the provision into the Maine Revised Statutes, the information will be searchable and findable. As an
experienced user of legislative and statutory research tools; I never think of looking in the Private and Special Laws, and you have to know exactly what you're looking for and where to find it. I tried the other day to access this section of law and could not--the Session Laws available online only go back to 1995. There is no impact to state employees, and the only textual changes are the stylistic and conventional draft changes
the Revisor's office makes when updating older sections of law.
Thank you for the opportunity to testify, I am happy to answer any questions you may
have.
10057657:
Colleen Brown Whiting LD 2093
Dear Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government,
My name is Colleen Brown and I am writing to submit written comment in support of LD 2093, regarding temporary disability for state employees.
I have a family member who works for the State of Maine on a DOT bridge crew. This is physically demanding work, often performed in difficult weather conditions and high-risk environments. Injuries and medical issues are not hypothetical in these roles, they are a real and ongoing risk.
Temporary disability protection matters because it helps keep working families stable when an employee is unable to work for a period of time due to an injury or medical issue. Without adequate protection, employees can be forced to burn through accrued time, go without pay, or face financial hardship at the exact moment their focus should be on recovery and returning to work safely.
Measures like LD 2093 support employee retention, reduce long-term disruption, and demonstrate that Maine values the workers who maintain essential infrastructure.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Respectfully submitted, Colleen Brown Whiting, Maine

LD 2093, An Act to Codify and Update a Provision of Private and

Before the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government
Senator Baldacci and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local
Government, I am Sue Salisbury, and I represent House District 128, which includes part of
Westbrook. I am here today to present LD 2093, An Act to Codify and Update a Provision of Private and Special Law Governing Temporary Disability for State Employees on behalf of
the Department of Administrative and Financial Services.
LD 2093 repeals a provision of private and special law governing temporary disability for state
employees and enacts that provision, with minor changes, in the Maine Revised Statutes.
Thank you for your consideration. There are representatives from the department who will
follow my testimony, and they will be able to answer any questions you may have.
